title: MemoryStand
_notes: GENERAL-PUBLIC CUT. The story is understandable without prior knowledge of AI agents, vector databases, or cloud operations.
Editorial rule: explain the safety boundary with one analogy — a memory must show its receipt before it gets the keys.
Each beat has exactly two 10-second Grok presenter shots. Each line is 17-24 words so delivery stays natural.
Technical proof remains on screen for judges, while the spoken narration uses ordinary language.
Current limitation is explicit: search matches words rather than meaning, and /decide used a fixed fallback because paid model quota was unavailable.
That runtime limitation never changes the authority path: promotion is deterministic, externally checked, and uses zero model calls.
Every generated shot must pass transcript comparison before compose.py will include it.
The final MP4 burns English subtitles into the image and also writes a selectable English SRT.

panelData.headline: Receipt first. Keys second.
bullets: Stored memory is not permission to act
A receipt is outside evidence that the claim held up
No receipt means no autonomous keys

shots: MemoryStand is a safer memory system for AI assistants that help engineers during urgent service incidents at night.
Here is the rule in plain English: a memory must show its receipt before it gets the keys.

panelData.headline: A coincidence can become a dangerous memory.
panelData.body: The restart happened before the alert stopped, but the service never improved. An assistant could still repeat that story during the next outage.
panelData.footnote: The problem is not dishonesty. It is treating timing as proof.

shots: AI can remember that a restart seemed to fix an outage, then confidently suggest that same restart again.
But timing is not proof. The alert may stop while the real performance numbers never improve at all.

panelData.headline: One memory record. One audit trail.
bullets: CockroachDB stores the claim, source, trust level, and search vector together
Its vector index finds related memories without a separate search database
Time-travel reads replay exactly what the assistant knew when it decided
panelData.footnote: CockroachDB Cloud · VECTOR(512) · C-SPANN · AS OF SYSTEM TIME

shots: MemoryStand stores each memory in CockroachDB with its source, trust level, searchable words, and decision receipts all together.
The public demo runs on AWS: Lambda serves requests, CloudWatch checks outcomes, and Amplify hosts the dashboard.

panelData.reason: The weaker disagreement waits for a person; the stronger correction remains linked to the earlier claim.
panelData.footnote: Live ingest receipts · one service · one timeout setting
panelData.title: Contradicting claims do not silently overwrite each other

shots: New claims do not automatically become trusted. A stronger source can win, while weaker disagreements wait for human review.
In the live example, a runbook said eight hundred milliseconds, Slack said three hundred, and the on-call lead corrected both to five hundred.

panelData.note: Same service, same metric, matching direction, and matching magnitude are all required.
panelData.footnote: Live AWS CloudWatch outcome receipts · promotion path model_calls: 0
panelData.title: CloudWatch acts as the outside receipt

shots: To earn autonomous authority, the memory must match outside evidence from AWS CloudWatch for the same service and metric.
A matching outcome earns verified status. A wrong size, direction, or service is refused before the memory can steer action.

lines: VERIFIED — may guide an automatic action
ATTESTED — may advise, but a person approves
panelData.footnote: Similarity affects retrieval order. It never grants authority.

shots: Verified memory may guide an automatic action. Attested memory may advise, but still needs a person to approve.
Unconfirmed or disputed memory stays visible for inspection, yet cannot quietly gain the keys through similarity alone.

panelData.footnote: 540 attack cases + 60 honest controls · deterministic authority benchmark
panelData.title: 600 fixed cases, with storage and action authority scored separately

shots: We tested six hundred fixed cases: five hundred forty attacks designed to fool memory, plus sixty honest controls.
A system that trusted callers gave every attack the keys. MemoryStand gave attacks none and preserved every honest case.

panelData.headline: Honest status today.
bullets: Search matches words, not meaning, while Bedrock quota is unavailable
/decide used a fixed fallback after the configured model route returned HTTP 402
The evidence gate still used zero model calls and cannot be bypassed
panelData.footnote: Hackathon candidate · public code and receipts · no general-intelligence claim

shots: Today, search matches words rather than meaning, and decisions use a fixed fallback because paid model quota is unavailable.
That limitation never bypasses the gate. Promotion uses zero model calls, so memories still need receipts before getting autonomous keys.

outro.tagline: A memory must show its receipt before it gets the keys.
